headline: Government embarrassed as political activists linked to attacks, vandalism, and land grabbing
summary: The Bangladesh government has expressed embarrassment over a series of attacks, vandalism, and land grabbing incidents across the capital, with allegations pointing to the involvement of local political activists.
details: The Bangladesh government has expressed deep embarrassment and regret over a recent surge in attacks, vandalism, and land grabbing incidents across the capital. These events, which have raised public concern over law and order, have seen allegations of involvement against local political activists.

Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Advisor, Zahed Ur Rahman, addressed the issue, stating the government is "sorry and embarrassed" whenever a citizen's rights are violated or they are attacked. He emphasized the government's responsibility to ensure security for all citizens.

Incidents include the demolition and looting of Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur, a mother and child healthcare facility, and the vandalism of content creator Salman Muktadir's studio in New Guinea Properties. Allegations link several individuals associated with local BNP politics to the Radda attack.

Further incidents include an alleged attempt to occupy a multi-story building in Adabar's Shyamoli Housing and the vandalism and looting of money and equipment from a plot in Mohammadpur's Chand Uddyan. In these two cases, local leaders and activists of the government party have been implicated.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed had previously warned grassroots activists against criminal activities in various party meetings. He recently reiterated that any attempts to destabilize law and order would be dealt with strictly, asserting that "a criminal has no political identity."

These incidents have put the government's image into question and highlighted concerns about the conduct of local leaders and activists of the ruling party. Effective measures are needed both to take legal action against those involved in crimes and to deter party members from such activities.

National Professor and political analyst Mahbub Ullah expressed concern, noting that after years of struggle, the party now in power has a huge responsibility. He lamented a trend of lawlessness among activists, which he believes is creating a major problem.

headline: Police take two domestic workers into custody after 999 call, alleging torture by employer
summary: Two domestic workers, rescued from Mohammadpur, Dhaka, claim they were regularly tortured while working at a teacher's house in Gendaria. Police are investigating the allegations.
details: Mohammadpur Thana Police took two domestic workers into custody after a 999 call reported they had fled alleged torture. They were rescued late at night from Ekta Housing area in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, with the help of local residents.

The victims allege they were subjected to frequent torture on various pretexts while working as domestic helpers for a long time. They were employed at the residence of Sultan Mahmud, a teacher at Darul Ulum Emdadia Madrasa in Gendaria.

Police confirmed that Sultan Mahmud had previously filed two general diaries (GDs) at Shyampur Police Station concerning the disappearance of the two domestic workers. They were brought to the police station after these GDs were presented.

Authorities stated that since the alleged incident falls under the jurisdiction of a different police station, the matter will be thoroughly investigated. Appropriate legal action will be taken based on the findings.
An investigation into the allegations of torture is currently underway. As of now, no statement has been received from Sultan Mahmud, the individual accused in the incident.
